requirements.evidence: Migrations match the task: unique slug (2026_10_29_042754_create_entities_table.php:17), FKs cascade, role default 'employee', storedAs owner_seq plus named uniques 'entity_memberships_entity_user_unique' and 'entity_memberships_one_owner' (…create_entity_memberships_table.php:16-26). Every model and enum contract is present, including UserRole::manageable() and User::membershipFor(int). The policies match the spec, including the membership delete rule that blocks the owner and allows self-removal (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:25-32). EntityController::pick uses Gate::authorize, then the session, then Log::channel('audit'), then a redirect. Members implements addMember (exists rule plus a duplicate error on email), assignRole validates role with Rule::in(manageable), and removeMember enforces the owner and last-manager rules. Settings implements save (unique slug ignoring itself), delete (soft delete, memberships, session) and transfer (owner lockForUpdate, admin target via whereKeyNot, demote before promote, 403 when the owner row vanished). Routes and lang keys are in both locales, and the dashboard shows the settings link to the owner only (@can('manageSettings')).

conventions.evidence: Authorization goes through policies, Members uses #[Validate] on $email, models use #[Fillable], migrations have down(), views use the existing <x-form-field>/<x-button> components and Bulma, and CHANGELOG, database-schema.md and business-rules.md are updated. However, every domain write (add/assign/remove member, update/delete entity, transfer ownership) is done directly in the Livewire components (Members.php:50, Settings.php:56,72-75,95-104). The conventions require these writes to go through app/Actions/* classes. Settings uses rules() rather than #[Validate], which the policy allows.

security.evidence: $entity is #[Locked] in all three components. Every public action re-authorizes ($this->authorize('update'|'assignRole'|'delete'|'manageSettings')). Membership ids are resolved through $this->entity->memberships()->findOrFail (Members.php:117), and the transfer target is resolved and filtered to admins of this entity (Settings.php:94-98). All output uses {{ }}, with no {!! !!}. The owner role cannot be reassigned (Members.php:71). No exploitable path found.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/EntityModelTest.php covers named indexes, the second-owner DB rejection, cascades, scopes, factories and policy matrices. tests/Feature/EntityPagesTest.php covers pick (happy path, 403 with session untouched, guest/unverified), dashboard visibility and translation, non-member 403, validation datasets, duplicate members, employee 403 on add/assign, cross-entity id tamper, locked entity swap, owner/last-manager removal, re-authorization after demotion for save/delete/transfer, the transfer target matrix (employee/self/foreign/missing/garbage) and the vanished owner. The entity-swap tests only assert a generic Exception, which is a weak assertion.

simplicity.evidence: The code is lean overall. roleOf()/isManager() are duplicated across EntityPolicy.php:43-50 and EntityMembershipPolicy.php:34-41. The test helpers member()/joined() are identical in the two test files. The last-manager guard (Members.php:84-89) can rarely trigger because an owner always exists.

readability.evidence: Methods are small and well named, with comments explaining non-obvious choices ('Demote first: the unique (entity_id, owner_seq) index…', 'Never trust the id sent by the client'). The code follows sibling style and has no dead code or debug output. removeMember lacks the PHPDoc that its siblings have.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task. Onboarding, the switcher, middleware and navbar changes are not included. The doc edits are limited to the entities and memberships sections that the task asked to update.

issues.explanation: Domain writes (adding/removing members, assigning roles, updating/deleting the entity, transferring ownership) are done inline in the Livewire components instead of in app/Actions/* use-case classes, as the conventions require.
The roleOf()/isManager() helpers are duplicated in both policies, and the test helpers member()/joined() are duplicated across the two test files.
The locked-entity tamper tests only expect a generic Exception, so they would also pass for unrelated failures; asserting the specific locked-property exception would be stronger.
The public $targetMembershipId is untyped and has no validation rule. It is safely resolved via filter_var and a scoped query, but it does not follow the 'validate public properties' pattern.
removeMember has no PHPDoc, unlike the other public actions.

review.summary: The change implements the entity data model with a DB-enforced single owner, the policies, entity.pick and the Livewire dashboard, members and settings pages, closely following the task contract. Server-side authorization, locked state and resolution of client ids are solid, and the tests are thorough, including tamper and unauthorized calls. The main deviation is that domain writes live in the components rather than in app/Actions classes, so I would approve after that refactor or with that acknowledged.
